newsitem.title: GERMANY: Breuer urges more pragmatic view on revaluations.
newsitem.headline: Breuer urges more pragmatic view on revaluations.

text.p: Rolf Breuer, the head of Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank AG, on Tuesday urged European governments to be more pragmatic when dealing with the issue of revaluing assets before currency union.
Asked to discuss the issue of revaluing national assets and privatising government owned properties or corporations, Breuer said nations should be able to use the same principles used in business.
"We should take a more pragmatic, a more realistic view," Breuer said discussing the fact that valuing assets close to market prices is a common business practice.

In a veiled reference to a debate raging in Germany about revaluing assets and using the proceeds to help fill budget gaps before currency union, Breuer said "we are too puristic, too idealistic, we should be more pragmatic."

The Bundesbank reacted strongly to plans on the part of the Bonn government to revalue its assets this year in a bid to raise extra funds in the final months before the qualification decision on monetary union.
Under a compromise deal, a partial upward revision of the value of the central bank's assets, which are currently on the books at well below market prices, will take place at teh end of this year.
